newsitem.title: USA: HCC Insurance to buy Avemco in stock swap.
newsitem.headline: HCC Insurance to buy Avemco in stock swap.

text.p: HCC Insurance Holdings Inc said Friday it had signed a letter of intent to acquire AVEMCO Corp in a stock swap valued at $230 million.
The acquisition will be non-dilutive to HCC's 1997 earnings and accretive to its 1998 earnings, HCC Chairman Stephen Way told Reuters in a telephone interview.
HCC, a speciality insurance group, is expected to earn $1.35 per share in fiscal 1997 and $1.77 in fiscal 1998, according to First Call.
Avemco underwrites specialty insurance, principally for small to medium-size aircraft operators.
HCC said it will exchange one share of its stock for each share of AVEMCO.

HCC had about 35.8 million shares outstanding as of December 31, compared with AVEMCO's 8.3 million. HCC will have about 44 million shares outstanding after the close of the acquisition, expected in June, Way said.
Avemco shares closed at 19-3/8 Thursday and HCC finished at 28-5/8. Neither had traded by late morning today.
"Avemco was not for sale," said Way. "We approached them. We felt there were some good synergies between us."

Way said AVEMCO'S position in the U.S. aviation insurance market would complement HCC's position in the international aviation market. He also said that in light of recent softness in the property and casualty market, the acquisition will help HCC continue its growth rate of more than 20 percent annually.
Way said HCC was on track to grow more than 20 percent in 1997. He did not make a specific estimate.
AVEMCO, which would operate as an independent unit of HCC, had revenues of $125 million in 1996.
After the acquisition, HCC will have a market capitalization of $1.3 billion, Way said.
AVEMCO Chief Financial Officer Jack Yuska said the transaction is subject to "an acceptable definitive agreement."
He refused to comment when asked if the company would entertain other offers or had received other offers prior to the one made by HCC. Yuska called HCC's offer "fair."
"In terms of looking at the deal on a one-for-one share basis, yes, it's a fair price," he said.
Harvey Bundy, an analyst at William Blair & Co, called the acquisition "an excellent move" for HCC.

He said it will give HCC a strengthened position in the U.S. private aviation market. He also said it will enable HCC to make more money in the reinsurance business because it gives LDG -- HCC's reinsurance arm -- a bigger market in many states.
He said a rival offer for AVEMCO from another insurance company was unlikely.
